Sam Choi: Quick question — I'm planning to work from Zurich for ~8 weeks (May 4–Jun 29). Do I need to do anything special for the WFH stipend / benefits / payroll / tax side?
Aisha HR: Thanks for the heads up Sam. Please fill out the short remote-travel form (link below) so we have dates + country. Stipend is prorated if >30 days.
Aisha HR: https://redwood.com/policies/remote-work (internal) — choose "Temporary international remote" and attach travel docs.
Sam Choi: Got it, filed form just now.
hr-bot: Received: remote-travel-form submitted by Sam Choi — ID #RWF-9841. People Ops will review within 2 business days.
Marco (Payroll): FYI — for Switzerland, anything under 90 days is usually fine for payroll not to switch, but it depends on canton rules and if you keep US tax residency. We need to confirm whether Redwood has any local payroll obligations. Please reply with exact travel dates and confirm you'll remain on US bank details.
Sam Choi: Dates above. Staying on US bank account, same benefits enrollment.
Priya (Legal): Quick legal note: short-term work (<=90 days) often doesn't trigger permanent establishment, but there are nuances: client-facing activity, local contracting, or paid work for local entity can change it. For safety, don't do any local contracting or sign terms under a Swiss entity. I'll loop in local counsel for Zurich to confirm.
Lena PM: Thanks Sam — approved from my side. Please keep working hours mostly overlapping with PST hours. :thumbsup:
Aisha HR: Stipend note: WFH allowance covers home office expenses; temporary travel stipend for coworking/short-term housing is considered a relocation/ad hoc benefit and may be taxable. We'll confirm gross-up options.
Marco (Payroll): Also need to check social security implications — even if payroll stays US, contributions can differ. I'll coordinate with our payroll vendor and update by EOD Thursday.
Priya (Legal): Looping in local counsel: @ZurichCounsel (external) — can you confirm: 1) whether Redwood needs payroll registration for an employee physically working in CH for 8 weeks; 2) any visa/permit issues for a US passport holder doing remote dev work.
ZurichCounsel (external): Quick reply — typically no permit if under 90 days for remote work, but canton may differ. Payroll registration usually not triggered for pure telework under 90 days. Recommend keeping documentation of dates and ensuring no local contracting.
Sam Choi: Great, thanks all. Anything else I should do pre-departure?
Aisha HR: Please set the "Out-of-country" field in Workday, attach the travel form ID, and confirm emergency contact. We'll also send a short checklist (health insurance top-ups, local emergency numbers).
Sam Choi: Done in Workday and added emergency contact.
Marco (Payroll): Noted. I'll post a follow-up in this thread with any payroll paperwork if needed.
Priya (Legal): I'll circulate the counsel note and one-pager on compliance best practices for short international remote stints.
Lena PM: Safe travels! Send pics. :camera_with_flash:
Sam Choi: Thanks team — appreciate the quick responses :raised_hands:
